pages.text:
Newton’s cooling equation

pages.title: Monotone versus oscillatory decay
pages.text:
Monotone versus oscillatory decay
0 < kh ≤ 1 : un preserves sign and decays ,
1 < kh < 2 : un alternates sign while decaying .
The second behavior is numerically stable but inconsistent with monotone cooling in this
model.

pages.title: Interpolation error for cooling
pages.text:
Interpolation error for cooling
T (t) − ~T (t) = T ′′(ξ)2 (t − ti)(t − ti+1).
Cooling from above ambient has T ′′ > 0. The product is nonpositive inside the interval,
so the secant lies above the exact curve.

pages.title: Sensitivity in time
pages.text:
Sensitivity in time
At t = 0, the temperature is independent of k. At very long times it is nearly ambient and
again weakly sensitive.
For t > 0, the magnitude te−kt is largest at t = 1/k.
Measurements near that scale are informative about k.
